Pattern Lab — Leaf & Lineage

PLAY ONLINE
https://ragingaxolotl-art.github.io/leaf-and-lineage/pattern-lab/

TEACHER SETUP
https://ragingaxolotl-art.github.io/leaf-and-lineage/pattern-lab/?teacher=1
Create a student link with chosen seed, mutation, tank cleanup, bedding permission, sumo permission and full-stat visibility.

PLAY OFFLINE
Open Pattern-Lab.html in a modern browser. It includes all code and artwork, without installation.
For a local server, serve this folder and open index.html. No dependencies or build step are needed.

BEETLE STORE
Open Beetle store beside the tank controls to see five random arrivals. Choose up to two per breeding round for free. Click a portrait for a larger view and raw measurement table, following the class statistics permissions. Hidden gene copies stay hidden. Five new arrivals appear after each successful breeding round; repeated sibling broods count as separate rounds. Reopening, reloading and tank-file saves keep the same stock and choices. Acquired beetles join the tank (or nursery when full), keep their exact displayed appearance, and follow normal cleanup. Move favorites to Keep before breeding. The stock has an independent random stream and does not change offspring rolls. No account or connection is needed.

TANK SPACE AND TRADING
An empty main tank and nursery can always be refilled: use Add starter beetles on the board or Fill empty tank with random beetles. You get 16 starters even during the five-cycle wait or with zero store picks. Keep favorites and jar parents remain. The store allowance and round counter do not reset. The normal five-cycle replacement wait returns once the working tank is occupied. Clearing saves a before-clear beetle recovery snapshot first.
Each successful brood saves its actual beetles before the birth is shown. Saved beetles & copies retains ten brood rosters and collected-opponent snapshots. See saved beetles lets you bring back one specimen with its exact genes without replacing your current tank. Save beetles now is a manual device checkpoint; Save tank file requests a portable download. Check Downloads for file completion. Replace tank with random beetles makes a before-replacement beetle snapshot. The original pre-upgrade save remains accessible when present.
Device saving uses IndexedDB, including trade checkpoints and sharing capabilities, avoiding the small localStorage tank limit. Existing saves migrate without deleting their source. Saved copies offers recovery versions. Wait for Saved on this device before leaving; a warning means a tank-file download is needed. Keep the same browser, website and class link to reopen that save.
Refresh tank · random beetles asks before releasing all main-tank and nursery beetles, including named/excluded beetles, and adding 16 fresh random founders. Keep favorites and jar parents remain. The breeding round, records, settings, notes and store lineup/pick allowance remain. Refresh and New tank unlock after five successful breeding cycles; each refresh starts another five-cycle wait, saved on this device and in tank files. Finish pending trades first. Save favorites or a tank file before refreshing.
Choose Keep newest brood only or Keep two newest broods in Automatic tank cleanup. A setting change applies when the next brood is born. Older unsaved beetles leave automatically. The default is two broods. Keep tank favorites (10 maximum) and jar parents are protected. The starting group counts as a brood. Named beetles show upright name tags in both tanks and are automatically excluded from cleanup. Inspect a beetle to change its Exclude from cleanup checkbox. Exclusions survive tank saves and are not inherited by babies. Clear unsaved beetles opens a review list: exclude any beetles to leave in the tank, then confirm deletion. Cancel changes nothing. Family labels and measured trait data remain; retired beetles cannot be selected again.
Share with a classmate lets both students keep their original beetle and receive an exact copy of the other offered beetle. Create a trade code, your friend enters it and offers theirs, then the creator previews and confirms. Both devices receive the exact genes and appearance, while both originals remain in their existing tanks. Refresh both screens and create a new sharing code for copy sharing; existing pending swaps retain their original rules. Use the original device until complete. Offers expire after two hours; collection receipts last seven days. Internet is required for codes. Keep your own tank file backup.

HOW TO PLAY
1. Click a beetle to inspect it without stopping the tank. Add 2–4 parents to a jar.
   Drag beetles to place them in either tank. Holding stops only that beetle.
   Release resumes movement; Cool & pause stops both tanks until Run is selected.
2. Check Use this jar. Breed selected jars makes 10–20 babies total.
3. With two jars, the babies split between them. Each baby's two parents come from its own jar.
4. New babies wander in the breeder tank. Overflow waits in the nursery.
5. Move up to 10 favorites to the separate Keep tank. Later broods never replace them.
6. Choose descendants as parents for later generations, or keep breeding the original group.
7. Save tank file or Save Keep tank + family file downloads the whole experiment.
   Open tank file restores the file, including favorites, genes, names, parentage and notes.

TRAIT MAGNIFIER
Below the breeder tank, choose up to three traits by opening the Trait 1, 2 and 3 dropdowns or typing to filter. Turn on Trait magnifier, then hover over a beetle in either the breeder or Keep tank. A small card shows its name, portrait and the selected readings. It switches to the next beetle as you move and closes when you leave the tank. Movement continues. Keyboard focus also shows the card. Strength is available in the magnifier for every class as an expressed 0–1 model value. Full-stat classes and teacher labs can choose additional expressed factors; other students get the existing measurable notebook traits, Strength and visible forms. No hidden gene copies are exposed. Other slots omit traits already selected, and unmatched searches leave the previous selection in place. Clicking a beetle still opens its inspector.

FLIPS AND FASTER ARENA MOVEMENT
Arena walking is 40% faster, with 20% faster acceleration and 15% faster turning; inherited differences and growth tradeoffs remain. This changes new matches only; old replays retain their original movement. Missing visible horns prevent horn lifts entirely. Tiny nubs have very low success, lift duration and flip odds; inherited lift talent cannot replace the missing anatomy. Jumping requires expressed spring joints and puffing requires expressed puff glands. Successful horn lifts have a separate flip roll that increases continuously with lift height. Horn reach, power and control help, while grip and balance resist. Flipped beetles cannot push or use moves and have 20% of normal support until they right themselves. Recovery, legs, mass and body growth affect a roughly 1.1–5 second righting period. Afterward, a 1.5 second flip grace period prevents immediate repeat flips. No health bar or injury is involved. New matches use SUMO8; rooms use SUMO8X2/SUMO8X10 and negotiate the host’s speed automatically.

GRAPPLING ADAPTATIONS
Horn lift, spring jump and bombardier puff are harmless automatic sumo actions, with wind-ups, energy costs and recovery delays. Lifts briefly reduce grip and need frontal positioning; horn reach helps, while low bodies, grip and bracing resist. Jumps escape contact and puffs but cannot push while airborne; poor landing control can cause a ring-out. Puffs need range and aim, briefly scramble movement/pushing, and have two charges per match. All effects end completely after each match. No KO or health bar is used.
Each move has six gradual quantitative factors: power, reach, control, efficiency, recovery and use instinct. Spring joints and puff glands have rare recessive structure gates: nn expresses, N masks. New founders have a 0.2% expressed chance and a 2.5% carrier chance for each structure, using an independent deterministic founder stream. Gate mutation is 1% of the classroom per-copy rate. Once discovered, actual inherited copies can retain the structure in a family. Original saved beetles upgrade with absent structures and midpoint ability factors; existing DNA and pending-trade fingerprints remain intact. Anatomy does not ensure correct use. Colors and patterns keep inherited surprises.

SUMO AND SHARING
Choose red and blue beetles, then Start local match. Pause or adjust playback without changing the outcome.
Tracking, reaction, focus, ring tactics, speed, grip, mass, bracing, balance and instincts are inherited spectra. Sustained pushing uses muscle, alignment, grip and energy; speed helps approaching and circling. All 77 continuous anatomy and behavior values use a many-gene breeding-value approximation. Babies normally stay near the parents’ average with small variation up or down. Most mutations are small; occasional larger effects can shift a value further. The classroom mutation setting controls frequency. Existing beetles retain their stored values. Appearance genes still pass real parental copies, so hidden colors and patterns can reappear. The field-mark tags are consistent clues to discover through observation. Full-stat class links retain explicit measurements. The smaller legal ring has concentric distance guides. A single ring-out wins immediately; at 60 seconds, or a simultaneous double exit, the closer beetle wins. Nearly equal distances can tie. Old match notebooks replay with their original rules; new shared matches require the current rules on both screens.
Front, side and rear pushes use different resistance. Wander-prone beetles may explore instead of pushing.
There are no injuries, deaths or gene changes from a match. The match notebook records replays.
To challenge another screen, expand Battle together on two computers. The host chooses its red beetle and creates a code.
The other child chooses their red beetle, enters the code and sends it. The host starts the shared match.
The red and blue Send to corner buttons match their corner colors. In shared rooms, a large Start friend battle button sits directly below the ring. It unlocks for the host when both beetles have joined; visitors see Waiting for host. After the match it becomes Start rematch. After a completed friend battle, Copy friend’s beetle to my tank adds the opponent with its exact genes and appearance, while your friend keeps theirs. This also works later from Match notebook, even after leaving the table or reopening the saved tank. Copies go to the nursery if the tank is full. Move favorites to Keep before breeding. Repeated clicks/rematches do not duplicate an existing live copy; an opponent can be recovered again if that copy has since left through cleanup. Both screens share a three-second countdown, the same fixed-step moves and the same result. The host chooses Shared match speed, either 2× or 10×, before creating a room. The visitor automatically adopts that speed. Sixty simulated seconds take thirty real seconds at 2× or six at 10× after the countdown. Speed stays locked for that room; leave and create a new code to change it. The countdown and six-second victory dance remain at normal speed. Both classmates should refresh the lab and create a new room code for synchronized 10× playback. Local playback remains adjustable.
The client corrects its clock using short server round trips; a screen returning from a background tab catches up.
Small timing differences remain possible on slow connections. The winner gets confetti and a short dance
on both screens, and the winning student sees Your beetle wins. Reduced-motion settings show a still celebration.
Each new match has fresh decision rolls. Rematches clear the old celebration.
Only the selected beetle's anonymous genetic packet is sent, not names, notes or the rest of the tank.
Codes expire in two hours. Create a new code to change the shared beetles. The code service needs internet.

STUDENT TRAIT NOTEBOOK
Overall body size is a continuous measurement derived as sqrt(inherited body length × inherited body width) × 2^bodyGrowth. Body growth can be selected from 1/8 to 4 times the baseline dimensions; inspector portraits fit the full anatomy while tank views preserve size differences. Those dimensions and body mass breed gradually; most babies stay close to the parental average, with rare larger mutations. Select descendants as new parents to accumulate changes over generations. Open trait notebook lets students choose one of 48 expressed measurements. Read a raw data table,
sort by generation or breeding round, and filter by parent jar or imported/local origin.
There are no graphs or precomputed summaries in the student notebook.
Repeated broods of the same parents are siblings in the same lineage generation. Each beetle counts once.
Download raw data CSV exports only that selected trait, never strength
or hidden gene copies. Displayed numbers round to four decimals; CSV keeps full stored precision.
Archived measurements remain after beetles leave and are saved in the tank file. Older missing records
are marked unavailable; they are not counted as zero or reconstructed. Dimensions use relative game
scales and indices, not real-species measurements. Body RGB channels use 0–255 values.

GROWTH, HORNS AND PART COLORS
New founders begin with horn nubs. Six log2 growth modifiers extend body, antenna, leg, horn, head and jaw dimensions gradually. Each parent contributes within 0.035 log2 units of its expressed modifier when mutation is off. Mutation for these modifiers runs at 15% of the classroom setting; only 1% of those events make a larger shift. Horn count and horn shape mutate at 2% of the classroom setting. Counts change one step at a time: single to double, double to single/triple, triple to double. Inheritance can make a rare discovery common in a selected family. Frameworks and hidden pigments transmit actual parental copies. Leg and thorax colors have separate paired pigment records; their visible brightness also uses appendageShade. Neither color gives a sumo advantage.
Larger bodies resist pushes but lose speed and agility. Extended appendages have modest benefits and costs. The arena compresses body-size differences to keep its fixed ring playable; tank size differences remain visible. Old match notebooks retain their original physics.
Family trees display beetle portraits. New archived records retain an appearance snapshot without a playable genome. Older unavailable pictures are marked clearly. The enlarged inspector preview stays visible while its details scroll.

SIMPLE TRAIT REPORT
In the beetle inspector, Simple trait report restores the familiar horizontal trait bars for movement, body dimensions and behavior. It shows expressed traits with readable values, not paired gene tables. Index bars use 0–100; dimensions use the current model range and their own units. Longer bars do not guarantee a better beetle. Download simple report creates printable HTML. Teacher labs can always open it; student links follow Show all genetics. The raw student notebook remains a table.

FULL GENETICS REPORT
The magnifying-glass button in the beetle inspector opens a dense technical report with all 110 paired records, both copies, expression values at stored precision, mutations, gate effects and derived traits. QNT records estimate many small genetic effects; MEN records transmit actual copies. Teacher labs can always open this report. Student links follow Show all genetics. Download full report creates printable HTML; raw beetle JSON remains importable.

PORTABLE BEETLES
In the enlarged inspector, Export beetle JSON downloads a single beetle. Export beetle document creates a
printable HTML document that embeds the same genetic packet. Import beetle file accepts either file and adds
the specimen without replacing existing beetles. Printing the document as PDF is for reading; keep HTML or JSON
for re-upload. Whole tank files and single beetle files use separate Open/Import controls.
Old Pattern Lab v1 tank saves keep their original five chromosome pairs; added traits are initialized once.

Movement speed controls playback only. Inherited walking speed is a separate genetic trait.
Cooling, scenery and decorations do not change genes. No predators or automatic mating.
Genetics, behavior and sumo physics are original teaching models, not real-species genetics.
Auto-save automatically reopens the last tank for this class link in the same browser and device. New tank remains an explicit confirmed choice. Different class codes have separate saves; a release-version update does not reset them. Download a file before leaving a shared computer or changing devices.
Class links share starting presets, not later babies or saves. Files contain the full genetic record.
